etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally a compound of あ (a, distal pronominal marker) + の (no, genitive particle).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Vowel shortening and gemination of みとうもない (mitōmonai), euphonic sound change of みたくもない (mitakumonai, “don't even want to see”) (via deletion of the intermediate /k/, a regular process in Japanese).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowing from English pass.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Clipping of カリパス (karipasu) or キャリパス (kyaripasu), ultimately a borrowing from English calipers.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowing from English path.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English sewing machine.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From ran (乱, disordered, confused, chaotic) + bō (暴, acting with destructive force).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: /konsiu/ → /konsjuː/

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Japanese shinjitai form: 僧 (曾 → 曽).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Clipping of 僧伽 (sōgya), borrowed from Sanskrit संघ (saṃgha).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 出来 (deki, the stem or continuative form of verb 出来る (dekiru), “to be able to do; be finished, be ready”) + 上がる (agaru, “to go up, come to an end”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 力(ちから) (chikara, “power, strength”) + 強(つよ)い (tsuyoi, “strong, powerful”). The tsuyoi changes to zuyoi as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 吐(は)き (haki, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 吐(は)く (haku, “vomit”).) + 気(け) (-ke, “feeling”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From お坊(ぼう)さん (obōsan).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 坊(ぼう) (bō, “boy”) + や (ya, interjectory particle). Compare 婆(ばあ)や (bāya), 爺(じい)や (jīya), 姉(ねえ)や (nēya). Resemblance to English boy is coincidental.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 夜(よ) (yo, “night”) + 明(あ)け (ake, “end (of a period)”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Despite the apparent overlap with the modern goon reading of oku that is derived from Middle Chinese, this term is actually rooted in Old Japanese, appearing in the Man'yōshū collection of poetry dating to roughly 759 CE. Cognate with 沖 (oki, “the open sea, offshore”), originally in reference to “somewhere far removed, possibly out of sight”. While oki came to mean “far removed in the wide open → far off shore”, oku instead came to mean “far removed inside → inside, interior”.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 學 (MC haewk, “learning”).
The goon pronunciation, so likely the initial borrowing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE.
Ultimately derived from classical verb 悔ゆ (kuyu, “to regret”), modern 悔いる (kuiru, “to regret”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Doublet of 推(お)す (osu).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: pir- > ɸir- > çir-. Cognate with verb 嚔る (hiru, “to sneeze”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: /papur/- → /ɸaɸur/- → */ɸawur/- → /ɸaur/- → /ɸoːr/- → /hoːr/-

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 最 (sai-, “most”) + 初 (sho, “new, first”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese. First attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE. From Proto-Japonic *makura.
Cognates
Cognate with Proto-Ryukyuan *makura, whence Kikai 枕 (makka), Kunigami 枕 (makkā), Miyako 枕 (maffa), Northern Amami Ōshima 枕 (makura), Okinawan 枕 (makkwa), Okinoerabu 枕 (makura), Southern Amami Ōshima 枕 (makra), Tokunoshima 枕 (makkwa), Yaeyama 枕 (maffa), Yonaguni 枕 (magura), and Yoron 枕 (makkura).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 焼く (yaku), in the 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) pattern. See the entry for further details.
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
First attested in the Kojiki of 712 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese. Appears in the Kojiki written in roughly 711-712. In turn, from Proto-Japonic *ta.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Ultimately from Middle Chinese 疑問 (MC ngi mjunH, literally “doubt, suspicion + ask”), apparently borrowed later as a learned borrowing from Literary Chinese of the same source term.
First attested in the early 1600s.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨puye⟩ → */puje/ → /ɸue/ → /fue/
From Old Japanese, first cited to the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.
Likely related to the verb 吹(ふ)く (fuku, “to blow”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 笛 (MC dek). The 漢音 (kan'on, literally “Han sound”), so likely a later borrowing.
First cited to a text from the 1400s. This reading appears to have fallen out of use.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From a corruption of Middle Chinese 笛 (MC dek).
First cited to a text from 1241.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: By surface analysis, 素(す) (su, “plain”) + 直(なお) (nao, “straight”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *untai. Cognate with Okinawan 腕 (udi).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From an original form kapina, reduced first to kaɸina, then kawina, then kaina.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *ti.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Clipping of 逆(さか)様(さま) (sakasama), of the same meaning.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 都 (to, “metropolis”) + 心 (shin, “central part”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 間(ま) (ma, “spatial interval, temporal interval”) + に (ni, “to, at”, indirect object particle) + 合(あ)う (au, “to match, to fit”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 集む (atumu), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
